stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s stock is up 0.9% today and 6.5% over the past month, trading just 1.3% below its 52‑week high and still 37.8% above its low. The modest pullback suggests the rally is nearing its peak, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of sustained momentum.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft gained 0.1% on the day and is up 7.2% month‑to‑date, sitting 1.5% shy of its 52‑week high while remaining 50.4% above its low. The key catalyst to monitor is the next quarterly earnings beat and any updates on its cloud growth trajectory.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA slipped 0.7% intraday but remains 0.7% below its 52‑week high and 44.1% above its low after a strong 5.3% monthly gain. Investors should focus on the upcoming AI‑related product announcements and inventory trends for the next price move.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet rose 0.8% today, trading 12.8% below its 52‑week peak yet still 48.5% above its low after a 3.6% monthly rise. The next driver will be the rollout of AI features in Search and any regulatory developments affecting its ad business.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon is up 1.4% on the day and 1.1% over the past month, currently 8.5% under its 52‑week high and 30.8% above its low. Watch the company’s Q3 earnings and any shifts in consumer spending trends for direction.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta fell 2.4% today, trading 7.2% below its 52‑week high after a 17.7% monthly surge. The upcoming earnings report and progress on its AI and metaverse initiatives will be critical for the next move.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla slipped 0.8% on the day, still 22.9% under its 52‑week high but 26.6% above its low after a 6.5% weekly gain. Investors should keep an eye on production updates and pricing strategy as the company seeks to reverse its YTD decline.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom rose 0.2% today, sitting 21.5% below its 52‑week high and 28.8% above its low after a 7.2% weekly rise. The next inflection point will likely be its quarterly earnings and any guidance on its semiconductor demand outlook.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD gained 0.5% on the day, trading just 0.5% shy of its 52‑week high after an explosive 189% YTD gain. The key watch is whether the momentum can be sustained post‑earnings, particularly around GPU and CPU market share gains.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle slipped 0.8% on the day and is down 11.7% month‑to‑date, sitting 53.7% below its 52‑week high but still 24.8% above its low, indicating a deep discount to recent peaks. The stock’s recent rebound of 4.6% over the past week suggests some short‑term buying interest. Investors should watch the upcoming earnings guidance for signs of a turnaround in cloud revenue.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce fell 0.2% today and is off 9.7% over the past month, trading 15.1% below its 52‑week high while still 49.9% above its low, reflecting a broad swing in valuation. Momentum remains negative with a 2.2% weekly decline. The key catalyst will be the next quarterly results, especially performance of its AI‑driven subscription suite.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan edged down 0.5% on the day but is up 3.2% YTD, trading 9.3% below its 52‑week high and 18.2% above its low, indicating modest resilience. Weekly movement is flat. Watch for net interest income trends and any shifts in loan‑loss provisions as rates evolve.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America slipped 1.1% and is down 14.2% over the month, sitting 17% under its 52‑week high yet 15.7% above its low, showing a broader pullback in regional banking stocks. Weekly performance is also negative. Investors should focus on the bank’s deposit mix and credit quality as the Fed’s policy path unfolds.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa rose 0.4% and is up 8.0% YTD, trading just 3.1% below its 52‑week high and 26.4% above its low, indicating it remains near the top of its range. The stock posted modest gains across the week and month. The next driver will be global payment‑volume growth and any updates on pricing power amid competitive pressures.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard gained 0.6% and is up 1.7% YTD, sitting 5.0% below its 52‑week high and 21.1% above its low, holding near the upper end of its range. Weekly momentum is positive. Watch for transaction‑volume trends and the impact of emerging‑market growth on fee revenue.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix climbed 1.5% on the day but remains 43.9% below its 52‑week high, though only 3.9% above its low, reflecting a steep decline from last year’s peak. The stock is down 9.2% month‑to‑date and 23.4% YTD. The upcoming subscriber‑growth report and any pricing changes will be pivotal.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly jumped 2.7% and is up 10.6% YTD, trading 7.2% below its 52‑week high and nearly 50% above its low, showing strong upside potential. It posted solid gains across the week and month. Investors should monitor upcoming FDA decisions and the pipeline’s impact on sales momentum.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth slipped 0.1% but is up 14.0% YTD, sitting 13.3% below its 52‑week high and 46.9% above its low, indicating steady strength. Weekly performance is positive. The key watch point is enrollment growth and cost‑containment measures in its Medicare Advantage business.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson rallied 1.4% on the day but remains 7.2% below its 52‑week high and 42.1% above its 52‑week low, reflecting a solid YTD gain of 26.6%. The recent bounce suggests resilience amid broader market weakness, but investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for any shifts in its pharmaceutical pipeline.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart is up 0.9% today, trading 19.2% off its 52‑week high yet only 8.4% above its 52‑week low, with a modest YTD decline of 3.5%. The stock’s incremental gains this week hint at steady consumer demand, while the key focus will be its same‑store sales trends and any impact from wage pressures.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco rose 0.7% on the day, sitting 13.8% below its 52‑week high and 11.3% above its 52‑week low, and is up 10.8% YTD. Momentum remains positive, but investors should monitor membership renewal rates and any slowdown in discretionary spending as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot slipped 0.3% intraday, still 25.3% under its 52‑week high but just 1.6% above its 52‑week low, with a YTD decline of 15.6%. The recent dip follows a broader market pullback; the upcoming housing‑starts data and DIY spending trends will be critical to gauge recovery.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil edged down 0.3% but stays just 3.1% shy of its 52‑week high and 52.6% above its 52‑week low, delivering a strong 36.4% YTD return. The stock’s performance hinges on crude‑price outlooks, so the next key watch is OPEC production decisions and U.S. inventory reports.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola fell 0.4% today, trading 6.2% below its 52‑week high and 33.2% above its 52‑week low, with a YTD gain of 26.6%. Investors should keep an eye on volume trends in emerging markets and any pricing adjustments as the primary driver ahead.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney rose 0.7% on the day, still 8.9% under its 52‑week high and 14.2% above its 52‑week low, with a YTD decline of 5.6%. The next inflection point will be the performance of its streaming segment and the rollout of its new park attractions.
